# Markederne balancerer på kanten - sådan ser erfarne investorer vejen frem

**Feed**: millionaerklubben  
**Published**: 2026-11-11  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

The Danish Millionærklubben episode (Euroinvestor, sponsored by Saxo Bank) has two guests: Michael Frisch Jørgensen of H.C. Andersen Capital and investor and economist Sten Jacobsen. They debate whether the market is turning risk-on or risk-off as AI optimism runs into hot US inflation, high interest rates and credit stress at heavily borrowed AI names like Oracle and CoreWeave. Their main thesis is that the AI capex boom depends on slow-to-build power grids and energy infrastructure that the bond market has to finance. That favours European power, grid and industrial names such as Vestas, FLSmidth, Iberdrola and Siemens Energy over the US hyperscalers. They also discuss Anthropic's IPO and how IPOs and fading buybacks drain liquidity from the market.

---

## Universe Stocks

### ⛔ CRWV — CoreWeave | **AVOID** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 80%

Michael calls it a terrible business model that cannot finance its expansion. Watch its debt spread, which did not tighten after results.

#### Reasoning

Guest Michael argues that the beat-and-raise does not matter because CoreWeave cannot fund its capex. It depends on bond-market financing with negative cash flow. Long-term survival is uncertain and the stock trades as a high-beta AI proxy. Sten adds that negative-cash-flow AI issuers are the credit risk to watch in 2027.

#### Sell Triggers

- if credit spreads tighten materially
- if a credible financing solution is secured

> *"Og det er jo en forfærdelig forretningsmodel."*

---

### ⛔ ORCL — Oracle | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Sten calls it the worst concept: an outdated system retrofitted for AI, funded by debt with negative cash flow. Bond rates are a key 2027 risk.

#### Reasoning

Guest Sten uses Oracle as the weakest link in his AI risk indicator. It issues heavy debt to build AI capacity on an outdated platform with negative free cash flow, and Microsoft reportedly pushed back on a contract. Its bond yields are a canary for the AI financing chain.

#### Sell Triggers

- if cash flow turns positive
- if Oracle bond spreads compress

> *"Oracle er uden sammenligning den dårligste koncept af en idé"*

---

### 🟢 VWS — Vestas | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Down 6% on Q3 miss, but Michael says ignore quarterly swings. Energy scarcity for AI could sharply lift turbine pricing.

#### Reasoning

Michael sees the Q3 miss as timing (Q2 was boosted by US tax-credit pull-forward) and urges looking through quarterly noise. He is convinced about the stock. The structural thesis is that the power shortage for AI data centres shifts returns to energy suppliers, so turbine prices could rise sharply. Both guests list Vestas among the European infrastructure beneficiaries.

#### Sell Triggers

- if order intake weakens structurally
- if turbine pricing per MW falls
- if supply chain issues persist

> *"luk nu bare øjnene for de her kvartalsvise bevægelser. Det er ret overbevidst om i den aktie."*

---

### 🟢 FLS — FLSmidth | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Strong results with order intake 6-7% above expectations. A raw-materials and AI build-out play that everyone wants to own.

#### Reasoning

Michael notes the solid report with order intake, a forward indicator, well above consensus. The AI build-out needs physical metals, so mining equipment demand should benefit. The stock had sold off on AI rotation, and the report brings investors back.

#### Sell Triggers

- if order intake slows
- if commodity capex cycle reverses

> *"så det er et solidt regnskab med en god fremadrettet indikator"*

---

### 🟢 IBE — Iberdrola | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Sten's old favourite power asset, which keeps performing. Power assets are underpriced relative to AI energy demand.

#### Reasoning

Sten's 90/10 model says the tangible economy must grow from 10% to ~25% of value to power AI. Power-generating assets are therefore likely too cheaply priced, and Iberdrola is his long-standing favourite in the theme.

#### Sell Triggers

- if regulators cap utility returns
- if AI power demand forecasts collapse

> *"Min gamle favorit, E-Pedrola, bliver ved med at gøre det godt"*

---

### 🟢 ENR — Siemens Energy | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Michael: if the energy and infrastructure story is right, you can only buy Europe: Siemens Energy, Siemens, Schneider, Vestas.

#### Reasoning

Europe kept its industrial and engineering base. The coming infrastructure build-out (grid, turbines) will be done by European companies, which supports a rotation away from US-heavy global indices.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the European infrastructure investment programme stalls

> *"Du kan kun købe Europa. Du har Siemens Energy, du har Siemens, du har Schneider, du har Vestas."*

---

### 🟢 SU — Schneider Electric | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Named as a European infrastructure and grid beneficiary of the AI energy build-out.

#### Reasoning

Same European infrastructure thesis from Michael. Grid electrification is the bottleneck, and the friction-reducing infrastructure suppliers capture returns.

#### Sell Triggers

- if grid investment slows

> *"du har Schneider"*

---

### 🟢 SIE — Siemens | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Named as a European industrial beneficiary of the infrastructure build-out.

#### Reasoning

Michael's European infrastructure list. Sten adds that the next decade will see the largest infrastructure investment in history, and European firms will build it in Europe.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the infrastructure capex cycle disappoints

> *"du har Siemens"*

---

### 🟠 HLUN-B — Lundbeck | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 50%

Clean beat on all fronts. The year-end patent-cliff decision is binary, so investors can no longer be underweight.

#### Reasoning

Michael highlights the strong report and the positioning ahead of the year-end decision on the patent cliff. Being underweight is too risky, but the outcome is binary.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the year-end decision confirms the patent cliff

> *"Folk kan ikke længere være undervægtede på den her, der er for stor risiko."*

---
